anchor: Wave motion and energy transfer > A travelling disturbance through neighbour interactions > Worked Example 1: Tracking a marked point on a rope: "The ribbon returns to rest at its original location once the disturbance passes."
title: Distinguishing Travelling Disturbance from Local Particle Motion
action: Select the option that correctly describes the motion of a travelling pulse compared with the motion of a marked ribbon tied to a rope.
prompt: A single upward wave pulse travels horizontally from left to right along a taut rope. A small red ribbon is tied securely to the rope at point P. Which statement correctly describes the motion of the pulse and point P?

options.text: The pulse travels horizontally to the right, while point P oscillates vertically up and down and returns to its equilibrium position.
Both the pulse and point P travel horizontally to the right at the same constant speed.
The pulse travels horizontally to the right, while point P remains completely motionless on the equilibrium line.
The pulse oscillates up and down in place, while point P travels horizontally along the rope.

feedback.A: Correct. The wave is a travelling disturbance that moves horizontally across the rope, while individual particles of the rope (and the tied ribbon) only oscillate locally perpendicular to the rope and return to equilibrium.
feedback.B: Incorrect. This reflects the common misconception that the medium travels with the wave. Point P is fixed to the rope fibres and moves only vertically; it does not travel horizontally with the pulse.
feedback.C: Incorrect. Point P cannot remain motionless when the disturbance arrives. Forces from neighbouring rope segments pull point P upward as the pulse passes, before restoring forces return it to rest.
feedback.D: Incorrect. This reverses the physical roles. The disturbance is what travels horizontally along the rope, whereas point P oscillates locally in place.

anchor: Wave motion and energy transfer > Mechanical demonstrations: ropes, springs, and ripple tanks > Worked Example 2: Comparing motion in a spring and a ripple tank: "Both systems transfer energy across space while their physical medium remains in place."
title: Comparing Local Medium Oscillation in Springs and Ripple Tanks
action: Select the row that correctly identifies the local motion of the medium when waves travel horizontally through a stretched spring and across a ripple tank.
prompt: A compression wave travels horizontally along a stretched helical spring, and a ripple travels horizontally across a ripple tank. How do the individual elements of each medium move as the wave passes?

options.text: Spring coils oscillate back and forth parallel to the spring; water elements bob up and down perpendicular to the surface.
Spring coils travel permanently to the far end of the spring; water elements travel permanently to the far wall of the tank.
Spring coils bob up and down perpendicular to the spring; water elements oscillate back and forth parallel to the wave direction.
Spring coils remain completely stationary; water elements stream continuously across the surface of the tank.

feedback.A: Correct. In a compression wave along a spring, coils oscillate parallel to the direction of propagation. In surface water ripples, water elements bob primarily perpendicular to the surface. In both cases, the medium elements oscillate locally about equilibrium.
feedback.B: Incorrect. Neither spring coils nor water elements are transported en masse to the far boundaries. The travelling disturbance passes forward, while the physical material remains in its local region.
feedback.C: Incorrect. In a longitudinal compression pulse along a spring, the coils shift along the spring axis (parallel), not perpendicular to it.
feedback.D: Incorrect. The coils must move to transmit contact forces to their neighbours, and water does not stream across the tank during the passage of small-amplitude ripples.

anchor: Wave motion and energy transfer > Progressive waves and energy transfer > Worked Example 3: Energy transfer without transport of matter: "The bobbing motion of the boat confirms that energy has reached the distant dock."
title: Identifying the Transferred Quantity and Physical Evidence
action: Select the statement that correctly identifies what a progressive wave transfers from place to place and cites valid experimental evidence.
prompt: Which statement correctly identifies the physical quantity transferred from source to receiver by a progressive wave, along with valid physical evidence?

options.text: A progressive wave transfers energy from place to place, evidenced by a distant floating boat gaining kinetic and potential energy to rock up and down.
A progressive wave transfers matter from place to place, evidenced by water piling up at the far end of a ripple tank.
A progressive wave transfers force from place to place, evidenced by particles remaining permanently displaced at the far boundary.
A progressive wave transfers neither energy nor matter, because all oscillating particles return to their original equilibrium positions.

feedback.A: Correct. By official Cambridge definition, a progressive wave is a wave that transfers energy from place to place. The work done in lifting and accelerating a distant floating object provides clear experimental evidence of this energy transfer.
feedback.B: Incorrect. Progressive waves transfer energy without any net transfer of the medium. Water does not continuously pile up at the far wall during normal wave propagation.
feedback.C: Incorrect. A wave exerts forces locally during interaction, but force is not the conserved entity transferred across space. Furthermore, particles return to equilibrium rather than staying permanently displaced.
feedback.D: Incorrect. Returning to equilibrium means net matter transport is zero, but energy was indeed transferred from the source to the receiver during the passage of the wave.

anchor: Wave motion and energy transfer > Two-track wave analysis: disturbance speed versus particle speed: "When a particle momentarily stops at its maximum displacement, the travelling wave pattern does not stop."
title: Contrasting Wave Propagation Speed with Particle Speed
action: Select the correct statement contrasting the speed of wave propagation with the motion of an individual particle of the medium.
prompt: A progressive wave travels horizontally through a medium at a constant propagation speed of 15 m s^-1. Which statement correctly describes the speed of a single particle in that medium?

options.text: The particle velocity continuously varies, reaching zero at maximum displacement and maximum value as it passes through equilibrium.
The particle moves constantly at 15 m s^-1 in the horizontal direction alongside the wave crest.
When the particle momentarily stops at its maximum displacement, the entire wave pattern momentarily stops travelling.
The particle maintains a constant vertical speed of 15 m s^-1 throughout its entire cycle of oscillation.

feedback.A: Correct. Two-track wave analysis separates the constant propagation speed of the travelling disturbance (15 m s^-1) from the variable velocity of an oscillating particle, which accelerates toward equilibrium and momentarily stops at turning points.
feedback.B: Incorrect. This confuses particle motion with wave propagation. Medium particles do not travel horizontally at the wave speed; they oscillate locally around equilibrium.
feedback.C: Incorrect. The wave pattern advances continuously at constant speed through the medium, regardless of where individual particles are in their local oscillatory cycles.
feedback.D: Incorrect. In simple harmonic or restoring oscillation, particle speed cannot be constant because restoring forces cause continuous acceleration and deceleration.

anchor: Wave motion and energy transfer > Single pulses and continuous periodic wave trains: "Successive particles along the string repeat the motion of the source with a progressive time delay."
title: Sequencing Particle Responses in a Continuous Wave Train
action: Select the option that correctly describes the response of three successive particles along a stretched string driven by a continuous vibration generator.
prompt: A vibration generator continuously oscillates the left end of a long horizontal string. Three marked particles, X, Y, and Z, are located along the string, where X is closest to the generator and Z is farthest. What describes their motion?

options.text: Particles X, Y, and Z all oscillate with the same frequency, but Y responds after X, and Z responds after Y due to propagation delay.
Particles X, Y, and Z all move in identical directions at the exact same instant with no time delay.
Particle X oscillates vertically, but the disturbance loses energy so completely that particle Z never moves at all.
Particle X moves vertically, particle Y moves horizontally, and particle Z remains permanently at rest.

feedback.A: Correct. In a continuous progressive wave train, successive particles repeat the motion of the source with a progressive time delay determined by the wave speed and their distance from the source.
feedback.B: Incorrect. Because the disturbance takes time to travel from X to Y to Z, adjacent particles cannot move in unison; they exhibit a progressive phase delay.
feedback.C: Incorrect. In an ideal continuous wave train, energy propagates continuously along the string so that distant particles like Z also oscillate once the disturbance reaches them.
feedback.D: Incorrect. All particles along the same uniform string undergo the same type of local vertical oscillation, rather than switching motion directions or remaining stationary.

anchor: Wave motion and energy transfer > Returning to Leonardo's wheat field and water ripples: "The water molecules bob locally around their resting positions without travelling with the wave crests."
title: Evaluating Experimental Claims on Floating Objects
action: Select the valid scientific deduction based on observing a small wooden block floating on water as progressive ripples pass by.
prompt: A student places a small wooden block on calm water in a long tank. A continuous train of progressive surface ripples travels from left to right past the block. Which observation and deduction is scientifically correct?

options.text: The block bobs up and down near its initial position, confirming that energy is transferred across the tank without net transport of water.
The block is carried rapidly from left to right to the end of the tank, proving that progressive waves transport mass across space.
The block remains completely stationary without moving at all, proving that surface ripples do not carry energy.
The block stays permanently fixed at a point of zero amplitude, proving that all progressive waves possess stationary nodes.

feedback.A: Correct. The bobbing motion proves that energy is transferred to the block by the arriving wave, while the lack of net horizontal drift demonstrates that water is not transported across space.
feedback.B: Incorrect. Real floating objects do not surf across the tank with small-amplitude progressive ripples; they oscillate locally around equilibrium.
feedback.C: Incorrect. The passing ripples disturb the water surface, exerting varying buoyant and pressure forces that force the floating block to bob up and down.
feedback.D: Incorrect. Fixed points of permanently zero amplitude (nodes) are characteristic of stationary waves, not progressive waves. In a pure progressive wave, all particles oscillate.
